chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Ibn Abi Najran from 'Asim ibn Humayd from Abi Basir from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) sent Ali (peace be upon him) to Yemen, and when he arrived, he said to him, 'Tell me of the most surprising thing that has happened to you.' He said, 'O Messenger of God, a group of men came to me who had bought a slave girl and all of them had intercourse with her in one period of purity, so she gave birth to a boy, and they all disputed over him, each claiming him. So I cast lots among them and gave him to the one whose lot came out, and I made him responsible for his share.' The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to him, 'Indeed, it is not the case that a group disputes and then entrusts their matter to God except that the lot of the one who is right (has the true claim) comes out.'

The Sheikh (may God have mercy on him) said: And it is not permissible for a man to sell a slave girl whom he has had intercourse with until she completes her istibra' (period of waiting to confirm pregnancy) with one menstruation or forty-five days. And likewise, it is not permissible for the one who bought her to have intercourse with her until she completes her istibra' in the same manner, unless the one who sold her is trustworthy and truthful, stating that he did not have intercourse with her since she became pure. This is indicated by what he narrated:

key_terms.اَلْمُحِقِّ: The one with the true claim/right

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a slave girl after intercourse and how is paternity determined in a dispute among multiple men?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *istibra'* (waiting period) and the mechanism of *al-gharar* (uncertainty) in lineage determination, where Ali (peace be upon him) used casting lots to resolve paternity disputes among multiple men. Al-Shaykh al-Tusi derives the legal requirement for a slave girl to undergo *istibra'* before sale or intercourse to ensure clear lineage, a foundational concept in Shia jurisprudence for establishing *nasab*. The Prophet’s affirmation that the lot falls to the 'true claimant' underscores the divine guidance in resolving ambiguous familial ties.
